newsitem.title: USA: Maryland approves BG&E, PEPCO merger.
newsitem.headline: Maryland approves BG&E, PEPCO merger.

text.p: Maryland Public Service Commission Wednesday approved the merger of Baltimore Gas and Electric Co and Potomac Electric Power Co on condition that the utilities reduce their rates.

To counter concerns that the $2.9 billion mrger to form Constellation Energy would be able to totally control the local power market, the commission required BG&E to cut rates to its customers by about $44 million and PEPCO to cut rates by more than $12 million.
After the rates are reduced, Constellation's base rates will be frozen for three years.
The commission also ordered the company to give customers half of any earnings it gained in excess of a 11.4 percent return on equity.
"The merger will allow the combined company to provide service more efficiently and effectively, and that the merger would produce financial savings that should be shared with ratepayers,"
The Maryland agency's decision on the union, which would create the tenth largest U.S. utility, came on the heels of an approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

While saying that the merger would not affect competition in the wholesale power market in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland power pool area, the federal commission raised concern about its impact on local consumers.

The FERC deferred to Maryland and District of Columbia regulators to address the issue of how to deal with Constellation's potential grip on consumers if local power markets are eventually opened to competition.
District of Columbia has yet to rule on the merger, which the two companies aim to complete before July.
